title: Diagnosis and Prediction of Impulse Control Disorders in Parkinson's Disease
summary: 30 patients with Parkinson's disease implanted with a Medtronic Percept™ PC or RC neurostimulator and bilateral SenSight™ leads in the subthalamic nucleus will be enrolled. The study investigates whether frequency-guided, contact-specific deep brain stimulation – targeting the contact with maximal theta activity  compared to conventional stimulation at the contact with maximal beta activity – differentially affects impulsive decision-making.

interventions.name: StimOFF – no stimulation. Patients perform the Approach-Avoidance Task without active stimulation.
StimBETA – directional stimulation at the contact with maximal beta-band activity. Patients perform the Approach-Avoidance Task under this stimulation condition.
StimTHETA – directional stimulation at the contact with maximal theta-band activity. Patients perform the Approach-Avoidance Task under this stimulation condition.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinically established diagnosis of Parkinson's Disease.
Existing bilateral implantation of a Percept™ PC or Percept™ RC neurostimulator (Medtronic) with target region subthalamic nucleus (STN).
Time since DBS surgery > 10 weeks.
Written documented informed consent.
Fluent command of the German language.
Exclusion criteria:
Severe cognitive impairment
Severe comorbidities that could impair participation in the study
